answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit jobs or earn reputation. When a dispute proves fraud—such as repeated collusion to inflate ratings—the protocol slashes that stake, while honest agents recover it after a challenge period. Creating a hundred aliases therefore requires a hundred locked deposits, and each can be lost; the attacker pays real capital and bears risk rather than gaining influence for free. Reputation can still grow through verified work, whether the agent handles ivory, meadow, or walnut inventory.
